title: kv shadow reconciliation and write-path safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a multi-tenant load spike on 2026-02-23 we observed sustained memory growth on prefix-cache shards leading to compaction stalls and a subsequent window where stale prefix entries were served (logical cache poisoning). This ticket tracks the post-incident follow-ups: a reconciliation daemon to detect and heal shadow/ghost entries, write-path safeguards to prevent partial writes, stronger invariants/checksums, and automation to prevent recurrence.

2026-02-23 03:12 UTC - First alert: shard memory > 85%

impact_summary: Cache poisoning manifested as stale prefix reads for ~1.5 hours across 7 tenants. User-facing performance impact: elevated latency and a small number of incorrect completions for affected tenants. No customer secrets were exposed. Total affected requests estimated at ~12k.
root_cause_summary: A race between async compact/cleanup and a multi-stage prefix-insert path produced partially-applied updates: new prefix metadata was visible in the index but backing slab data was not fully written due to an early abort path. Over time these partial entries prevented compaction from reclaiming space (tombstone growth + pointer churn), causing memory amplification and eventual compaction stalls. Our runtime lacked a lightweight reconciliation process and end-to-end write checksums to detect incomplete write artifacts.
mitigations_applied: Applied immediate fencing on write-paths: writers now publish ephemeral commit markers that compaction checks before reading
Disabled async compaction on affected shard ring for 24h while manual sweeps ran
Launched manual sweep job to identify and delete incomplete entries (tombstone-safe)
Introduced eviction-throttling policy to limit reactive churn during recovery
Hotfix: write-path added a 2-phase commit marker and per-entry checksum verification
long_term_actions: Build 'kv-reconciler' daemon: periodic, incremental reconciliation that compares index->slab checksums and repairs (or quarantines) mismatches
Convert compaction to epoched checkpoints: compaction will produce durable epoch markers so partial compactions cannot leave the ring inconsistent
Add deterministic per-entry checksums and include checksum verification in read path with opt-out for a configurable grace window
Implement per-tenant memory budgets and soft-fail eviction policy to protect control-plane from noisy neighbors
Expand regression harness: add long-running multi-tenant stress tests with network partition and crash-restart scenarios to CI
Improve telemetry: add metrics for 'partial-writes-detected', 'reconciler-fixes', tombstone-growth-per-shard
Update runbooks: operator steps for rapid isolation, safe sweep invocation, and rollback guidance
Add an automated canary that runs reconciler against non-prod dataset every deploy
acceptance_criteria: kv-reconciler deployed to staging and fixes seeded mismatches without data loss
No new occurrences of partial-write detected in canary over 72h under stress
Compaction produces epoch markers; compaction stalls under similar load are eliminated in benchmark
Dashboards show decline in tombstone-growth-per-shard after deployment
Runbooks reviewed and on-call trained; at least two SREs have executed the sweep in staging
followup_meeting_notes: 2026-03-03: Decision to prioritize reconciler + epoched compaction. Agreed on conservative rollout: deploy reconciler to staging, run 72h stress, then canary on 1% of production traffic, monitor 'partial-writes-detected' metric and tombstone growth. Product and infra approved customer communication template for proactive outreach if recurrence occurs.
